  \caption{Where \txn{7}'s saving went. Each bar is a transaction's weight times the change in its mean latency against \expt{b15}; they sum to the change in mean response time per transaction (net), and with no think time TPS $=$ clients $/$ response time, which predicts every measured ratio here within 0.2\%. The labels give the TPS change that \txn{7}'s latency alone would predict (top) and the measured change (bottom). At 64 clients \txn{1} and \txn{6} slow down by 0.98\,ms of the 1.53\,ms that \txn{7} saves in \expt{b19}, so the predicted +10\% becomes +3\%. \expt{b16} is left out: its \txn{7} adds 5.2\,ms at 64 clients.}
